task.description: Per WF-03 Step 4 and the design doc's §6 regression-test guidance: this defect is a compile-time --warnings-as-errors gate failure, not a runtime behavior defect, so the fail-then-pass regression proof is the compile gate itself run against pre-fix and post-fix code, not a new ExUnit test (the design doc explicitly recommends against an ExUnit-only substitute for this defect class, since ExUnit does not run --warnings-as-errors).
acceptance_criteria: Pre-fix: mix compile --warnings-as-errors fails with the exact 3 warnings reproduced in Step 1
Post-fix: same command exits 0 with zero warnings
Full test suite stays green post-fix, same pass count

result.summary: Fail-first proof executed directly (not merely described): `git stash push -- lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex` reverted the file to its pre-fix state, then `rm -rf _build/dev/lib/letflow && mix compile --warnings-as-errors` was re-run -- exit code 1, output ending 'Compilation failed due to warnings while using the --warnings-as-errors option', 3 warning blocks present (grep -c "warning:" on the captured output = 3), matching Step 1's original reproduction exactly (same 3 sites: dispatch_start/4 line 218 Token update, dispatch_end/3 line 235 InstanceState update, dispatch_human_task/3 line 246 InstanceState update). `git stash pop` restored the fix. Post-fix re-verification: `rm -rf _build/dev/lib/letflow && mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> exit 0, output 'Compiling 66 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warning blocks. This IS the regression test for this defect class -- a compile-gate command, run at both states, with real captured output at each -- per the design doc's own §6 guidance that an ExUnit test would not exercise --warnings-as-errors and would therefore not actually prove this specific defect's fail-then-pass behavior. Supplementary: since ISS-0046's own compile-gate defect is orthogonal to transition/3's runtime correctness, the existing test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs suite (already covering :START/:END/:HUMAN_TASK dispatch, unchanged by this fix) continues to demonstrate correct runtime behavior for the same InstanceState/Token values now also pattern-matched -- no new test needed there since no new behavior was introduced, only type-narrowing of already-guaranteed-well-formed inputs.
